meta.note: 仿真题，非真题原文。按真题「年份/场次/篇章」结构组织。
meta.structure: 六/四级听力：一卷含 Section A 短篇新闻(3篇) + Section B 长对话(2篇) + Section C 短文(3篇)。

sentences.cn: 跨学科教育鼓励学生将不同领域的知识联系起来。

sentences.en: The lecture will begin at nine a.m. in the main building.
sentences.cn: 讲座将于上午九点在主楼开始。

sentences.en: Please make sure to submit your assignment before the deadline.
sentences.cn: 请确保在截止日期前提交作业。

sentences.en: Researchers have found that sleep deprivation impairs memory formation.
sentences.cn: 研究人员发现睡眠不足会损害记忆形成。

sentences.en: The company adopted a new marketing strategy to attract younger consumers.
sentences.cn: 该公司采用了一种新的营销策略来吸引年轻消费者。

sentences.cn: 气候变化对沿海生态系统构成严重威胁。

sentences.en: Although the proposal seemed promising, it was ultimately rejected.
sentences.cn: 尽管这个提案看起来很有前景，但最终被否决了。

sentences.en: Regular exercise not only strengthens the body but also improves mood.
sentences.cn: 规律运动不仅强健身体，还能改善情绪。

sentences.en: The committee has decided to postpone the vote until next month.
sentences.cn: 委员会决定将投票推迟到下个月。

sentences.en: Students are encouraged to take part in international exchange activities.
sentences.cn: 学校鼓励学生参加国际交流活动。

sentences.en: What strikes me most about this policy is how little discussion it has generated.
sentences.cn: 这项政策最让我惊讶的是它引发的讨论如此之少。

sentences.en: The university plans to expand its research programs next year.
sentences.cn: 该校计划明年扩展其研究项目。

turns.en: Oh, I see. Is it open on weekends?
Yes, from nine to five on Saturdays and Sundays.

turns.cn: 那么，是什么促使你申请这个职位？

turns.cn: 我从事数据分析已经三年了，想承担更多责任。

script.en: Online learning has grown rapidly over the past decade. What was once considered a supplement to classroom teaching is now, for many students, the primary mode of instruction.
The most obvious advantage is flexibility. Students can attend lectures recorded at any time and submit assignments whenever convenient.
However, flexibility alone does not guarantee success. Research consistently shows that completion rates in online courses remain lower than in traditional classrooms.
The reason, most educators agree, is a lack of discipline and social interaction. Without a fixed schedule, students easily procrastinate.
Some universities have responded by redesigning courses around short modules with regular quizzes, which keeps students engaged week by week.
In short, online learning works best when it is structured rather than left entirely to the student's own time management.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the talk?
opts: To introduce a new research project
To explain the results of a recent survey
To compare online and classroom learning
To announce a change in university policy
qs.tip: 全文围绕线上学习与传统课堂的对比展开，注意首句与末句的总结句。

qs.q: According to the speaker, what is the most obvious advantage of online learning?
qs.tip: The most obvious advantage is flexibility 属于信号词句。

qs.q: What does research show about completion rates?
qs.tip: remain lower than in traditional classrooms，注意 remain 的语义倾向。

qs.q: Why do completion rates fall, according to most educators?
qs.tip: a lack of discipline and social interaction 是因果句。

qs.q: What have some universities done in response?
qs.tip: redesigning courses around short modules。

qs.q: What is the speaker's final point?
opts: Recordings are more useful than live lectures
qs.tip: works best when it is structured 是结论句。

script.en: Cities around the world are losing their green space at an alarming rate as land values rise.
This matters more than it may appear. Trees and parks reduce the heat island effect that makes urban summers dangerously hot.
They also support biodiversity, providing habitat for birds and insects that would otherwise disappear entirely.
Studies have repeatedly linked access to green space with improved mental well-being among residents.
Some city governments now treat green space not as decoration, but as essential infrastructure.
They are investing in rooftop gardens and restoring wetlands, even where land is extremely scarce.

qs.q: Why are cities losing green space?
qs.tip: as land values rise 是原因状语。

qs.q: According to the talk, one effect of trees and parks is to:
qs.tip: reduce the heat island effect 直接给出。

qs.q: What benefit do residents gain according to studies?
qs.tip: linked access to green space with improved mental well-being。

qs.q: How do some city governments now view green space?
qs.tip: not as decoration, but as essential infrastructure 是对比强调结构。

qs.q: What two measures are mentioned?
qs.tip: investing in rooftop gardens and restoring wetlands。

script.en: Municipal tree planting programmes have expanded rapidly in the past decade.
The stated goal is often to reduce carbon emissions, but the measurable effects are more immediate.
A mature street canopy can lower summer temperatures by several degrees, reducing the demand for cooling.
Leaves also trap particulate matter, and their roots absorb stormwater that would otherwise flood the streets.
Yet distribution remains uneven. Wealthier districts receive more planting than poorer ones.
Advocates argue that equity should be the starting point rather than an afterthought.

qs.q: What is the talk mainly about?
opts: Urban tree planting and its benefits
qs.tip: 首段给出主题，后段展开效益与公平问题。

qs.q: What can a mature canopy do, according to the talk?
qs.tip: lower summer temperatures by several degrees。

qs.q: What do leaves and roots do respectively?
qs.tip: Leaves trap particulate matter, roots absorb stormwater。

qs.q: What problem does the speaker mention?
qs.tip: distribution remains uneven 是转折后的问题点。

qs.q: What do advocates emphasise?
qs.tip: equity should be the starting point rather than an afterthought。

script.en: Modern technology has an undeniable capacity to make things faster.
Speed, however, is not always a benefit. In some settings it degrades the very quality it is meant to improve.
Consider medical diagnosis. A tool that returns a result in thirty seconds encourages clinicians to accept it without scrutiny.
The problem is not the tool but the incentive structure surrounding it.
Automation that removes human oversight removes accountability along with it.
Governments are beginning to require that a named human remains answerable for any automated decision.

qs.q: What does the speaker suggest about speed?
opts: It is mostly a marketing claim
qs.tip: Speed, however, is not always a benefit 是核心论点。

qs.q: What does the medical example illustrate?
qs.tip: encourages clinicians to accept it without scrutiny。

qs.q: Where does the speaker locate the problem?
qs.tip: not the tool but the incentive structure。

qs.q: What happens when human oversight is removed?
qs.tip: removes accountability along with it。

qs.q: What are governments beginning to require?
opts: A named human answerable for automated decisions
qs.tip: require that a named human remains answerable。
